12.head: 717eb58ec018a4c6f09a07e9d52e8920706d618b
12.feedback: {"head":"717eb58ec018a4c6f09a07e9d52e8920706d618b","verdict":"pass","summary":"The change adds a Node-only, read-only reporter (scripts/factory/diagnostics.cjs) invoked only on a failed Claude model step, which builds a bounded, allowlist-only JSON report (fixed tool names, fixed command categories/forms, counts, stop reason) from the pinned action's temporary execution file and uploads it under a separate \"diagnostic-<phase>-<grantId>\" artifact name with 7-day retention. Verified against the current source: the reporter is copied into $RUNNER_TEMP/factory-control before the untrusted ticket head is checked out (same trust boundary already used for worker.cjs), so it cannot be tampered with by ticket/repo content. It correctly distinguishes \"denials array present but empty\" (status=available, denialCount=0) from \"denials missing/invalid\" (status=unavailable, denialCount=null, explicit reason) — never fabricating a zero. File reads are bounded (8 MiB, re-checked after fstat to avoid TOCTOU growth), symlinks/directories are rejected via lstat+O_NOFOLLOW, and the output file is written with O_EXCL so a pre-existing file is refused rather than overwritten. Only three fixed-shape fields (tool, commandCategory, commandForm) ever leave the reporter per denial; raw commands/paths/prompts/IDs/errors are never included, verified by tests that smuggle a synthetic secret through every untrusted field and assert it never appears in the report, stdout, or stderr. The new workflow steps use `continue-on-error: true` and `if: failure() && steps.model.outcome == 'failure'`, so they only fire on an actual model-step failure, can't themselves flip the job back to success, and are skipped for preflight failures or cancellations — confirmed against factory-cycle.yml/factory-pr-review.yml, which gate on job `.result` unaffected by this addition. No other file (policy.cjs, worker.cjs, controller.cjs, permissions blocks, FACTORY_ENABLED gate, turn-ceiling logic) was touched. The new test file is automatically picked up by the existing `yarn test:factory` glob already run in CI, so no CI wiring changes were needed. Regression coverage is strong: missing/oversized/malformed/symlinked/directory inputs, truncation at 100 denials, PowerShell command classification, exact-vs-with-arguments vs compound/dynamic command forms, and non-overwrite of an existing output file are all exercised.","findings":[]}

14.feedback: {"head":"e117eb47a992b5be679f1da0db858e6ede25fda6","verdict":"pass","summary":"The diff raises FACTORY_MAX_TURNS_PER_RUN's ceiling to 50 and FACTORY_MAX_TICKETS_PER_DAY's ceiling to 5 in scripts/factory/policy.cjs's LIMITS table, with matching bound checks via the existing integer()/readConfig() validation (rejects 51/6 and malformed/missing values, same as before for the old ceilings of 20/2). New tests cover: turn budgets up to 50 remaining usable while preserving other caps; values above 50 or malformed being rejected; disabled/zero-turn budgets still blocking work; five admissions in one Bucharest day including an owner-PR review ticket, with a sixth ticket refused until midnight; and retrying an already-admitted ticket not re-admitting it or refunding its lifetime coding/retry counters. factory-worker.test.cjs confirms both coding and review CLI invocations carry --max-turns 50 without gaining extra tools. factory-controller.test.cjs's disabled validate-only smoke test and factory-ci.yml's CI fixture both exercise 50/5 with FACTORY_ENABLED=false, no token, no state writes, and no inference, matching the \"ordinary CI without inference or real credentials\" criterion. docs/CLAUDE-FACTORY.md documents the rollout sequence (stay at 20/2 until the policy PR is reviewed on trusted main, then move to 50/5 with the factory still disabled) and the follow-on issue #11 controlled-retry plan, without actually triggering any model session, merge, or live ledger change. All other policy invariants (15-minute timeout, 2 coding attempts/1 retry, 2 reviews, 1 concurrent ticket, OAuth-only subscription auth, review gate, PR #13 diagnostics) are untouched in the reviewed code. I did not find any violation of policy boundaries, scope creep beyond the two ceilings, or evidence that live credentials/state were touched.","findings":[]}
